clue.text: One of 8 left house to spot endless celebs

parts.note: to house troops is to quarter them, give them lodgings

indicators.note: the synonym for spot loses its final letter

parts.note: to spot something is to find it
the A-list is the top tier of celebrities

explanation.surface: Someone lodges their household so they can go celebrity-spotting.
explanation.walkthrough: The '8' is a number, not a cross-reference: eight competitors are left in the round before the semi-finals.
explanation.definitionFit: Eight players or teams contest the round before the semis, so each is one of eight left in the tournament.

clue.text: Forces people to take food here

definitions.text: Forces people to take food here

parts.words: Forces people to take food here
parts.note: reads like a place that makes people eat, but Forces means the armed services, whose personnel eat in a canteen

explanation.surface: Somewhere compels people to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forces' looks like a verb; it is the noun for the army, navy and air force.
explanation.definitionFit: A military canteen is where service personnel take their meals, so it fits the cryptic reading exactly.

clue.text: It's a bit of a fiddle kicking animal out of shelter

definitions.text: It's a bit of a fiddle

indicators.note: kicking something out removes it, here the beast from the dugout
says which word the beast is expelled from, the synonym for shelter

parts.note: a foxhole is a soldier's dug-in shelter
an ox is a farm animal

explanation.surface: A fiddle, or swindle, involving evicting a creature from its refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' suggests a swindle; it is a violin. Taking OX from FOXHOLE leaves FHOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The f-shaped sound holes cut in a violin's belly are part of the instrument, literally a bit of a fiddle.

clue.text: Arrange to return foil after school

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the abbreviation for school
return means the synonym for foil is read backwards

parts.note: to foil pursuers is to elude them

explanation.surface: Planning to bring back a fencing foil after lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' suggests a fencing sword or kitchen foil, but here it is the verb meaning thwart or evade.
explanation.definitionFit: To schedule something is to arrange it for a set time, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Move along before she drops hot pasty on the counter

indicators.note: the turned-round piece comes before what remains of she
counter here means running against the normal direction, so the synonym for pasty is turned round

parts.note: a pasty complexion is pale

indicators.note: the word she drops a letter for hot

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A shop assistant drops a hot Cornish pasty on the counter and must move on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the counter' turns PALE into ELAP; 'drops' takes H from SHE, leaving SE. A Cornish pasty is a British baked pastry filled with meat and vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: When time elapses it passes, moves along, so the verb matches the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Dresses prior to breaking legs

indicators.note: the word for prior to breaks into the synonym for legs, splitting it

parts.note: pins is slang for legs
afore is an old word meaning before, prior to

explanation.surface: Getting dressed before an accident that breaks legs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dresses' looks like a verb but is the plural noun; 'legs' gives the slang PINS, which 'breaking' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinafores are sleeveless dresses or aprons worn over clothing, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Medical support left around noon

indicators.note: the synonym for left goes around the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: split is slang for left, departed

explanation.surface: Someone left their medical aid lying around at midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' wraps SPLIT around N.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigid strip holding a broken bone still is a classic form of medical support.

clue.text: Actors inside get moving with these

definitions.text: Actors inside get moving with these

indicators.note: moving means the letters of the first three words are set in motion and rearranged

explanation.surface: Performers on set get going thanks to instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges the fifteen letters of ACTORS INSIDE GET. Read whole, the clue also describes the instructions in a script that tell actors where to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The italic instructions in a playscript tell performers when to enter, exit and move about the boards.

clue.text: I ate lunch drunk — wicked!

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of a boozy lunch as if it were outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Unethical conduct is morally wrong, and wicked also describes morally bad behaviour.

clue.text: Popular place for data

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A trendy spot for storing information.
explanation.definitionFit: Information fed into a computer is called its input, so the noun names the data entered.

clue.text: Sort out will

definitions.meaning: to settle or fix a problem

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means settle a problem; as a noun it means firm determination, the same as will.

clue.text: Insect makes monk sit up

parts.note: a monk is a man devoted to prayer, a praying man

indicators.note: in the down light the word sit is written upwards, so backwards

explanation.surface: An insect turns a monk into someone sitting upright.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half sits in the down light 20, so 'up' works as a reversal there.
explanation.definitionFit: This green predator holds its forelegs folded as if in prayer, a well-known insect.

clue.text: The spirit of Ireland

indicators.note: of signals that the letters come from within the word Ireland

explanation.surface: A question about Ireland's national character.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is flair, dash and vigour, a lively spirit shown in action.

clue.text: Refuse to do jumps like a mountain goat?

indicators.note: the letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: An animal declines to perform leaps, unlike an agile goat.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the goat as an example of the quality, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Mountain goats are famed for keeping their footing on steep crags, never stumbling.

clue.text: Indicated empty lavatory in a very obvious way

parts.note: to indicate something is to point it out

indicators.note: emptying a word leaves only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone gestured at a vacant toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only L and Y from LAVATORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something pointedly makes its meaning unmistakable, deliberately obvious.

clue.text: Cloying smoke envelops orchestra

indicators.note: the synonym for smoke wraps around the orchestra's initials

parts.note: fume is smoke or vapour
LSO is the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: Sickly smoke wraps around a concert orchestra.
explanation.walkthrough: The London Symphony Orchestra is usually known by its initials, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise is excessive and flattering to the point of being sickly, much like something cloying.

clue.text: Provided backing before churchman's slip, perhaps

indicators.note: the turned-round piece comes before the church official
backing means the word for provided is turned round

parts.note: if means provided that
an elder is an official of a Presbyterian church; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A clergyman's mistake gets supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI. In cricket the slips are close fielding positions behind the batsman, so 'slip' is the example.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket slip is one of the close catching positions, so the player stationed there is an example of this.

clue.text: Plant some after a hot spell

indicators.note: the word for some comes after the bout of high temperature

parts.note: a fever is a bout of high temperature
few means a small number, some

explanation.surface: A gardener sows something after a heatwave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hot spell' suggests weather; it is an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverfew is a daisy-like herb traditionally used against headaches, a plant.

clue.text: Crooked Shakespearean character enters country from the south

indicators.note: the villain goes into the reversed word for country
in a down light, read from the south means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a land is a country
Iago is the villain of Othello

explanation.surface: A dishonest Shakespeare villain invades a nation from below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crooked' looks like a description of the villain, but it is the definition, meaning slanting. The reversal gives DNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something crooked is slanting rather than straight, as a slanted line running corner to corner is.

clue.text: Resident has no time to pack case

indicators.note: the local person packs the other pieces inside, as into a suitcase

parts.note: a native is a local resident
O, zero, means none
min is short for minute, a unit of time

explanation.surface: A local is too busy to pack a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests luggage; it is the grammatical case.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the subject of a verb takes the nominative, one of the noun cases in Latin.

clue.text: See 12
Cheap metal sink

parts.note: tin is a metal
to pot a ball in snooker is to sink it

explanation.surface: A low-cost metal kitchen basin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot describes something shoddy and inferior, second-rate and cheap.

clue.text: Mineral starts to transform and loses colour

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: A mineral changes and fades.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft magnesium silicate mineral, the softest on the Mohs hardness scale.

clue.text: First Lady accepts Bill's fudge

indicators.note: the first woman takes in the short word for bill

parts.note: Eve, in Genesis, is the first woman
an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A president's wife takes her husband's sweets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife; it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To fudge an issue is to dodge or sidestep it, avoiding a straight answer.

clue.text: Fleet left before first light

indicators.note: first says the abbreviation for left and the word for before come ahead of the navy

parts.note: ante is Latin for before
RN is the Royal Navy, Britain's fleet

explanation.surface: A fleet sets out ahead of dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet' suggests ships setting sail at first light, but 'first' only tells you to put the other two pieces ahead of the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a portable lamp in a case, a kind of light.

clue.text: Food for Roman artist, one carrying instrument

indicators.note: the artist and one carry the instrument between them

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
I is the Roman numeral one
a viol is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A painter in Rome is fed while lugging a musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman artist' looks like one phrase; Roman belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are stuffed pasta parcels, Italian food fit for a Roman.

clue.text: Refuse second preference

parts.note: will can mean wish or preference

explanation.surface: Turning down a second choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb; it is the noun for waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill is kitchen waste fed to pigs, so it is a kind of refuse.

clue.text: Last kipper tie in range is exaggerated

indicators.note: the last letter and the tie go in the cooking range

parts.note: a range is a cooking stove, an oven

indicators.note: Last picks the final letter of kipper

parts.note: a draw is a tied game

explanation.surface: A smoked fish and a tie on the stove sound overdone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper tie' reads as the wide 1970s necktie, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn portrait is depicted with too much emphasis, overstated, so exaggerated.
